title: How Much Experience Should Your Scarsdale Architect Have?
excerpt: Choosing an architect for your Scarsdale home project matters more than you might think. Here's what real experience looks like and why it matters for your project.
content:
If you're planning a renovation, addition, or new build in Scarsdale, you've probably started thinking about who to hire. And if you're like most homeowners, you've wondered: what counts as real experience? How much is enough?

This is a fair question. Not all architects are the same, and the experience level you choose will directly affect how your project runs and how happy you are with the result.

What Does Experience Actually Mean?

When you're looking at an architect's background, don't just count the years. Look at what they've actually built. Have they done work in your town? Do they understand your specific neighborhood? Have they managed the full scope of projects like yours?

A licensed architect in New York needs to meet real standards. That's non-negotiable. But licensing is just the starting point. The question is whether they've spent years putting that license to work on real homes in real communities like Scarsdale.

In Scarsdale, you're dealing with a specific kind of property, specific town codes, and homeowners who care about detail. An architect who's worked in Scarsdale before knows these things in their bones. They've already solved problems you might face.

The Value of a Design-Build Approach

Here's something that matters more than most homeowners realize: does your architect actually understand construction? Some architects design beautiful things on paper but have never had to build them. They don't think like builders.

When you work with a design-build firm in Westchester, you get someone who speaks both languages. Silvio Luca, the principal at House Architecture & Construction, is both a licensed architect and a licensed general contractor. He personally runs every project. That's not common. It means the person designing your home addition in Scarsdale is the same person managing the crew that builds it.

This approach cuts through a lot of the back-and-forth that kills other projects. There's no finger-pointing between the architect's vision and what the contractor thinks is buildable. It's one person, one vision, from start to finish.

Experience With Your Specific Project Type

Ask your architect what they've actually done. If you want a second-story addition, have they built one before? Have they designed a primary suite addition? Have they renovated kitchens in homes like yours?

A residential architect in Scarsdale who's done multiple kitchen and bathroom renovations, home additions in Westchester, and historic restorations brings skills that matter. Each project type teaches you something the next one needs. Someone who's done fifteen kitchen remodels won't make mistakes that a first-timer might.

Look for someone who's also comfortable with the less flashy work. Open-concept conversions. Historic restorations. These aren't trendy projects, but they're harder than they look. Experience here tells you the architect thinks carefully about structure, codes, and what actually works.

Why You Should Call
